I reproduced this live against main and it is WORSE than the report says, so the 'minor' severity does not stand. Measured on the shipped seed with tenant_demo set to 'usd': /opportunities first row reads 'value ₹6,000.00' (as reported) and the page carries six rupee amounts, / carries six, /experiments carries four, the Qualified CPL tile reads '—', GET /v1/metrics reports spend_micros 0 with qualified_cpl_micros null, and POST /v1/events 400s CURRENCY_MISMATCH on a legitimate USD spend. Same for 'Usd' and ' USD ' — byte-identical pages, measured. The blast radius is still narrow and the trigger is external: normaliseGrowthEvent validates ingest currency against ISO_CURRENCIES exactly on both the body.value path and the pre-normalised payload path (src/domain/measurement.js:124 and :136), and routes.js seeds a new tenant's currency from that validated code, so nothing the app itself writes today produces a non-canonical code. The bug is that the read path is not defensive about a row it did not write (a human UPDATE, a legacy import, a future write path). THE CORRECTION CARRIED SINCE v1, restated because three reviews have now each found a different instance of the same arithmetic slipping: the em-dash on the SHIPPED SEED is not the defect and this order does not claim it is. The seed's only spend row (evt_seed_journey_spend_1) carries currency 'INR', amount_micros 7_200_000_000 (scripts/seed.js:21-25), and there are three seeded lead_qualified rows (:41-55). So a tenant whose spend rows are all genuinely foreign correctly sums to nothing and correctly renders the em-dash — that is computeFunnel's foreign-currency exclusion working (QA BUG-2), not a canonicalisation failure. What the defect removes is the case where the tenant's own unit of account and its own spend agree and the spend is merely LABELLED differently from the row: there the exclusion drops the tenant's real spend, the CPL goes null, and the ingest path 400s a legitimate event. ON THE OBJECTION TO v4, which was mechanical and which I did not dispute: AC-6 and qa_script step 10 pinned an arrow-const grep for the new helper name to 1, while this same order's tests[] case 1 instructed the implementer to write a function DECLARATION — so the string the criterion greps for could not exist in the file the order tells the implementer to write, and the count would print 0. I take the objection's option (a), the smaller edit and the one its own text calls sufficient on its own: the greps change to the declaration form, matching the `function usdRepos` style grep (3) and the instruction already use, and the today-count is re-measured below against unmodified main. The consequence of the disagreement is not cosmetic: it is the same defect class that sank v3, mirrored — v3 pinned the OLD closure name to a count its own refactor removed, v4 pinned the NEW name to a count its own refactor also removes. This version fixes the pair, writes the rejected arrow form in words and never in text (reproducing it here is how a work order certifies a string it does not contain — I made that mistake while drafting this version and removed it), and then greps its own text for every occurrence of the identifier to confirm one syntactic form appears and one form only; the check and its measured result are recorded in evidence below and in how_to_verify for AC-6. v5 changes nothing else about the design: the objection was about the work order's arithmetic, not about canonicalising the stored row.
work_order.root_cause: One exact-match membership test standing in for currency identity, at every point where a STORED TENANT code is read. A tenant code is stored as an arbitrary string (tenants.create takes any string; the column is TEXT), but three consumers compare it by exact string equality: money()'s ISO_CURRENCIES.includes guard at src/web/pages.js:222, computeFunnel's tenant-currency exclusion as fed from src/web/pages.js:377 and src/api/routes.js:170-171, and the CURRENCY_MISMATCH check at src/api/routes.js:145-150. 'usd' and 'USD' name the same unit of account, so all three treat the tenant's own spend as foreign and either relabel it or drop it. Nothing canonicalises between the row and those comparisons. The asymmetry that makes the fix safe: the tenant row is the only untrusted side of every one of these comparisons. The other side — an event's payload currency — is already canonical, because normaliseGrowthEvent rejects anything outside ISO_CURRENCIES exactly before the row is ever compared to it. So canonicalise the stored row, never the event payload, and never inside computeFunnel.
work_order.approach: Add one exported boundary function to the domain — canonicalCurrency(code) in src/domain/money.js, which trims and upper-cases a stored string and returns the ISO 4217 code it names, or null when it names none ('ZZZ' and 'XTS' still resolve to null, so the documented bad-data INR fallback and the never-500 behaviour are unchanged). Then resolve every read of a tenant row's currency through it, in one seam per module, rather than touching the comparisons individually: pages.js gets a local tenantCurrency(tenant) helper used at all EIGHT `tenant?.currency ?? 'INR'` / `tenant.currency ?? 'INR'` read sites (measured on main: 326, 346, 377, 390, 744, 758, 833, 849), and money() itself canonicalises before the fallback so any value that reaches the renderer by another path still draws its own unit. routes.js gets a local resolveTenantCurrency(row) helper used at both reads of the row — the metrics funnel filter and the CURRENCY_MISMATCH check — with the comparison canonicalising while the 400's message and details keep reporting the stored string verbatim, so every existing 400 is byte-identical and only the mis-cased tenant changes from rejected to accepted. The name is resolveTenantCurrency and not tenantCurrency deliberately: src/api/routes.js:170 already declares `const tenantCurrency = ...` inside the metrics handler, and a same-named module function would be shadowed there and a self-referential `const tenantCurrency = tenantCurrency(row)` would throw a TDZ ReferenceError. computeFunnel is NOT changed: it keeps its exact string comparison and is simply fed a canonical code, because its event-payload side is already guaranteed canonical by ingest. That is also what keeps the QA BUG-2 foreign-currency exclusion intact — a 'usd' tenant must still exclude a genuinely INR spend row, and a new test now pins that so a future implementer cannot 'fix' the em-dash by summing foreign spend; AC-4 makes the same exclusion observable at a live URL. Read-side only, deliberately: the QA repro sets the column with raw SQL UPDATE, which never touches tenants.create, so a write-side fix would not have fixed the reported case; and the existing test at test/web/pages.test.js:1077-1080 pins tenants.create accepting any string, so tightening the write path would break a deliberate contract for no gain on the reported defect. Separately, close the two review findings in the same test file: lift the repeated tenant+opportunity block into a usdRepos() helper beside freshRepos()/seededRepos() and the repeated envelope closure into one tenant-parameterised validatedEnvelope(tenantId, event_id, event_type, payload), and have all three call sites use them; and extend the fixture guard to assert the resolved spend amount alongside the qualified-lead count, so a broken numerator fails at the guard with a fixture-shaped message instead of surfacing at the money assertion as an em-dash. Both new helpers are FUNCTION DECLARATIONS, which is the syntactic form the four AC-6 greps pin — this is the single point v4 got wrong and it is now consistent in tests[], in AC-6 and in qa_script step 10.

assumptions: Trim-and-upper is the right canonicalisation for ISO 4217 codes, and no tenant needs a code that is legitimately mixed-case or padded. ISO 4217 codes are upper-case alpha-3 by definition, so the mapping is total on well-formed input and a no-op on canonical input.

A mis-cased or padded tenant code is bad data, not a distinct unit of account, and no tenant row anywhere in the wild holds a code that canonicalises to something other than what was meant. The only sources are a human UPDATE and a legacy import; the app's own write path already emits canonical codes.

The stored tenant row is the only side of every currency comparison that needs canonicalising. The event-payload side is validated exactly at ingest on both paths into the payload, so there is no second untrusted spelling to handle.
unknowns: Whether any deployed database outside this repo holds a non-canonical tenant row. Nothing in the repo enumerates tenants beyond the demo one, and the read-side fix makes such a row render correctly whether or not it exists, so the answer does not change the work — it changes only whether QA ever sees the bug in the wild.

Whether a tenant row could ever legitimately hold a currency outside ISO_CURRENCIES that this build should still render. The 'ZZZ' test says no: unknown is bad data and INR is the documented fallback. This ticket does not revisit that decision, and qa_script step 7 keeps that control live. One measured consequence to be aware of: a 'ZZZ' tenant's GET /v1/metrics spend_micros changes from 0 on main to 7_200_000_000 after the fix, because the fallback is now applied consistently to the metric as well as to the renderer — so AC-3 deliberately asserts no metrics number at 'ZZZ'.
residual_risks: A stored code that is mis-cased AND a currency with no 2-digit minor unit now renders in its own unit for the first time, where before it drew rupees. If any such row exists, the numbers a reader sees will change currency on upgrade. That is the fix, not a regression, and no test asserts the old value for such a row — but QA should read the first AC-1 render as a deliberate change rather than a diff to be accepted at a glance.

A non-canonical row stays non-canonical in storage after this change. It renders correctly everywhere now, but the next reader of the tenants table sees 'usd' and may reasonably assume the app normalises on write. It does not. The fix is stated at the read boundary in the money() doc comment, which is the only place a future implementer is likely to be looking.

Because raw_events is append-only, an operator who realises a tenant row is mis-cased cannot repair the affected spend rows once they have been written in the wrong unit — the events stay foreign and stay excluded, and the CPL stays null. The read-side fix makes such a row render its own currency for everything else, so the remaining wrongness is confined to the funnel, and correcting it means new events rather than an edit. This is a property of the existing append-only design, not something this change introduces, and it is a reason the silent canonicalisation is acceptable rather than a reason to widen the ticket.

A refactor whose correctness is pinned to grep counts depends on those counts being checked, not assumed. If a future change adds a second legitimate closure-shaped fixture, grep (1) stays 0 and grep (2) stays 1 while the file grows a new builder under a different name — the criterion proves the two named fixtures were not duplicated, not that the file has exactly one fixture builder. That is the claim AC-6 actually makes and the one worth making; a stronger claim would need a different check and is not proposed here.
